newsitem.title: USA: G7 leaders warn against "harmful" tax competition.
newsitem.headline: G7 leaders warn against "harmful" tax competition.

text.p: Leaders of the Group of Seven industrial nations have warned againt the dangers of countries competing with each other to attract financial investments by offering special tax breaks.
In a draft of a statement to be issued later on Saturday, the leaders said that tax competition between nations could distort trade and erode the ability of individual countries to raise taxes.
"The globalization of national economies has increased the challenge of harmful tax competition," the draft statement said.

"Tax schemes aimed at attracting financial and other geographically mobile activities can create harmful tax competition between states, carrying risks of distorting trade and investment, and could lead to the erosion of national tax bases," it added.
The statement appeared to be referring to offshore tax havens, some of them poorly regulated, which attract billions of dollars of savings from the world's richer nations.

Leaders encouraged the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), which groups leading industrialized nations, to come up with proposals to tackle a problem which "undermines the fairness and neutrality of the tax system."
"We hope that the OECD can produce its conclusions and recommendations on this subject in time for our conideration at next year's summit," the statement added.
